Chapter 7: Breaking the Cycle—Becoming a Parent.
Imagine this—you're holding your own child for the very first time. Suddenly, a wave of love and protectiveness just washes over you. It's thrilling... and honestly, a bit terrifying. You want, more than anything, to give your child the safety and stability you always wished for. But those old fears? They don't just disappear. What if you slip up? What if you repeat the mistakes your parents made? What if, somehow, the darkness sneaks back in?
Every day, parenthood tests your patience and self-awareness. There are times when frustration just bubbles up, and you feel that urge—to control, to pull away—almost like it's second nature. In those moments, you catch yourself. You remember the promises you made to do better. So, you lean into vulnerability. You apologize when you fall short. You reach out for help when you need it. It's not always easy, but it's real.
With your partner, you talk openly about your childhoods. About the patterns you both want to leave behind, and the values you hope to pass on. Together, you build small rituals—reading bedtime stories, sharing family dinners, taking quiet walks in the park. These simple things become anchors. They remind you that love doesn't have to be chaotic. It can be steady, and safe.
Of course, the past still shows up from time to time. Maybe it's a harsh word, a slammed door, or just a silence that lasts too long. In those moments, you feel the old panic rise—the fear that you're turning into your father. But then, your child reaches for you, eyes full of trust and no fear at all. And right there, you remember: you can choose differently. Every single day is a new chance to offer the kindness and understanding you always needed.
Watching your child move through the world, it's hard not to feel a sense of wonder. They're open. They're at ease. Sure, there are challenges—every family has them. But that old cycle of fear and secrecy? It's been broken. That's something to be proud of. You know just how much it took to get here.
Your biggest hope is that your child will never have to carry the same burdens you did. But if they ever do, you'll be there. You'll help them find their way.
In the end, parenthood becomes a kind of redemption. It's your chance to rewrite the story—to offer the love and safety that once felt out of reach. The scars from the past might still be there, but they don't get to decide what comes next.
